name: osteoarthritis overview
title: Osteoarthritis as a chronic monoarthritis: rule out red flags, make the clinical diagnosis, stage it on X-ray, then treat with biomechanical and education measures at every stage, medicines for symptoms, and joint replacement only for end-stage disease; arthroscopy is not recommended

root.title: ONE joint aching for over 6 weeks, worse with activity: osteoarthritis (OA) until a red flag says otherwise
lines: OA is a CLINICAL diagnosis: typical symptoms + NO other cause · the X-ray STAGES it, it does not diagnose it
first set aside mechanical and sports causes of knee pain (no arthritis)

chronic monoarthritis: OA, OA, OA, then chronic crystals (gout, pseudogout, basic calcium phosphate) · less often autoimmune, Charcot (diabetes, syphilis), chronic infection (atypical mycobacteria), tumour (pigmented villonodular synovitis, synovial chondromatosis), osteonecrosis
1 in 7 Canadian adults · most common joint disorder · 11th cause of disability worldwide (above TB, heart disease) · knee OA mostly starts at 35-55

groups.title: IS IT OA?
lines: knee >> hip; ankle; shoulder >> big toe · hand, thumb base usually with polyarthritis

groups.title: TREAT IT: what stage, what can be fixed?
lines: no treatment preserves the joint; all improve life WITH it

head: h
Red flag → NOT OA
think something else
clue: • warm or hot joint: infection, crystals
tx: MRI or bone scan only when the diagnosis is in DOUBT

head: h
Osteoarthritis
a 'sick joint': every tissue fails to heal
clue: case: 52 F, type 2 diabetes, knee pain since 45, 5 min stiffness, cool swelling, joint-line tender, crepitus
• post-traumatic OA starts young · case: 36 F, ACL tear at 23 → > 50% need a knee replacement by 55

head: h
Every stage: biomechanics + education
alignment · overuse · weakness · gait
clue: • neuromuscular exercise physiotherapy, ≥ 3 months (Tai-Chi, GLA:D program)
• 150 min of activity a week (walk, swim, bike)
tx: • occupational therapy: joint protection, avoid risky movements

head: h
Medicines: symptoms only
less pain, better function
clue: • oral NSAID if no contraindication (not in kidney failure)
• refractory: steroid injection (short-term), then a duloxetine (SNRI) trial 2–3 months
case: 68 M, varus knee, chronic renal failure → physio 3 months, OT, TOPICAL NSAID (no oral), injection, duloxetine
tx: • glucosamine, herbal remedies · topical NSAID for HIP OA
• injected hyaluronic acid, platelet-rich plasma, stem cells
• opioids: generally avoid (tramadol at most; others: risks > benefit)

head: h
Surgery: END STAGE only
unacceptable symptoms despite all of the rest
clue: a salvage procedure · strong evidence of benefit
• X-ray bone on bone → refer to orthopedics
case: same man 2 years later, cane, bone on bone despite all → knee arthroplasty
tx: ± meniscectomy or repair: no meaningful benefit

panels.title: Primary vs secondary OA
items: primary (most): risk factors, no clear cause
secondary: post-traumatic (ACL, meniscus tear) · acromegaly, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis · rare monogenic (Stickler, Marshall, dysplasias) · after rheumatoid or other inflammatory arthritis

panels.title: Why OA happens
items: NOT wear and tear or age: cartilage thins with age, raising the risk
chronic metabolic, mechanical stress → inflammation, pain, breakdown of every joint tissue
joint FAILURE, like heart failure: tissues fail to heal · treat what impairs healing (obesity, inactivity)
